claims.text: A spray-deposited 2D (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflake coating with a high-temperature adhesion promoter will maintain low friction and wear on CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
Bare CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing friction and wear with increasing temperature.
Oxidation and adhesion-related degradation are the primary causes of the elevated-temperature tribological deterioration of bare CoCrFeNi.
The 2D (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 material can be applied by air-spray coating.
Spray deposition will produce a uniform nanolayer of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 on CoCrFeNi.
A high-temperature adhesion promoter or diffusion barrier can be incorporated into the nanoflake coating on CoCrFeNi.
The enhanced coating will promote formation of a continuously renewing nanocrystalline glaze layer at the sliding interface.
The adhesion promoter will preserve coating integrity at temperatures up to 800 °C and loads up to 9 N.
Sliding stress activates tribocatalytic behavior in 2D (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes.
Localized high temperatures contribute to activation of the proposed tribocatalytic reactions.
Tribocatalytic reactions in the coating generate a self-adaptive lubricious film on CoCrFeNi.
The lubricious film may contain carbonaceous species derived from residual contaminants or solvents.
The interfacial protective film will reduce adhesive and oxidative wear.
The adhesion promoter will prevent coating delamination and thereby sustain generation of the protective film.
The enhanced coating will produce a coefficient of friction below 0.1 across room temperature to 800 °C under loads from 1 to 9 N.
The enhanced coating will reduce wear rate by at least one order of magnitude relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full temperature range.
The intervention will remain effective in ambient or simulated operational atmospheres between room temperature and 800 °C and between 1 and 9 N.
Long-term coating phase stability during sustained exposure at 800 °C is uncertain.
Adhesion-promoter performance under cyclic or dynamic loading is uncertain.
